channel.description: Recent content in Posts on How We Got There

item.title: Credits & Doors Out
item.description: Credits due first — published sources, existing interactives, and images this journey stands on

item.title: Foreword
item.description: An interactive journey from relays to attention — not an encyclopedia

item.title: Pattern cards on silk
item.description: Swap the cards, change the flower — the weaver’s hands stay the same

item.title: The barrel organ
item.description: It does not know a hymn — pegs decide the song

item.title: The caravan
item.description: Agreed marks on clay or cloth — the marks and stops are clever, not the caravan

item.title: The desk clerk
item.description: Marks, a written list of steps — and a person who can tire, skip, or guess

item.title: The feast scoop
item.description: Same measure every guest — never a deeper scoop for the tenth plate

item.title: The player piano
item.description: Holes in a roll; the same roll twice is the same piece

item.title: The stubborn helper
item.description: Never bored, never guessing, never “improving” the request

item.title: The water wheel
item.description: A fixed chore you can trust — the wheel will not improvise

item.title: Trays of pebbles
item.description: Three trays, a recipe card one step at a time, and an answer strip

item.title: What is this thing?
item.description: Nine doors into the same idea — pick any, then meet the brass engines

item.title: Babbage's Engines
item.description: Difference Engine and Analytical Engine — store, mill, and a program on cards

item.title: The Jacquard Loom
item.description: Punched cards made a program separate from the machine that runs it

item.title: Why Mechanical Computing Matters
item.description: The logical shape arrived in brass; friction forced electricity

item.title: Relays and Electromechanical Logic
item.description: Relays proved binary logic works — and that moving metal cannot keep up

item.title: The Vacuum Tube Era
item.description: Tubes removed moving parts — and traded that speed for heat, power, and failure

item.title: Why the Transistor Had to Happen
item.description: Size, power, reliability — three tube ceilings that made solid-state switching inevitable

item.title: Semiconductors from First Principles
item.description: A band gap you can push either way — doping turns silicon into a controllable switch

item.title: The Transistor: BJT to MOSFET
item.description: Current-controlled BJTs burned idle power; voltage-controlled MOSFETs made density possible

item.title: Logic Gates from Transistors
item.description: CMOS pairs NMOS and PMOS so idle gates draw no static path — the topology that scaled

item.title: From Gates to Combinational Logic
item.description: Compose gates into adders and an ALU — then hit the carry-ripple delay that forces better structures

item.title: Sequential Logic
item.description: Feedback makes bistable memory; edge-triggered flip-flops make synchronous design tractable — until setup/hold caps the clock

item.title: The Memory Hierarchy Begins
item.description: Flip-flops are too expensive per bit — SRAM buys speed, DRAM buys density, and the hierarchy is the tradeoff repeated

item.title: Instruction Sets
item.description: The ISA is the software–hardware contract; CISC and RISC are two answers to what that contract should look like

item.title: Datapath Design
item.description: A single-cycle datapath makes the pieces visible — and shows why its clock is sized to the worst case

item.title: Pipelining
item.description: Overlap instructions for throughput — then hazards force forwarding, stalls, and everything that follows

item.title: Branch Prediction
item.description: Pipeline flushes are expensive — prediction exists to make them rare

item.title: Caches
item.description: Locality makes the memory hierarchy work; associativity and coherence are the costs of keeping it honest

item.title: Out-of-Order Execution
item.description: Stall only what must wait — Tomasulo’s idea: execute when ready, commit in order

item.title: Superscalar & Multicore
item.description: ILP and power hit walls — so the industry went wide instead of faster per thread

item.title: Mainframes to Minicomputers to Microprocessors
item.description: Three eras of who gets a computer — institutional, departmental, then one chip for everyone

item.title: The x86 vs RISC Split
item.description: RISC was cleaner on paper — software lock-in and µop translation kept x86 on top

item.title: ARM and RISC-V: The Architecture Landscape Today
item.description: After desktop settled on x86, the fight moved to power and licensing — ARM won mobile; RISC-V bets on open

item.title: Batch Processing and the Birth of the Operating System
item.description: Expensive CPUs sitting idle between punch-card jobs forced the first resident monitor — system software, not a user’s program

item.title: Time-Sharing and the Unix Lineage
item.description: Batch kept the CPU busy; time-sharing gave many users the illusion of owning it — Multics ambition, then Unix simplicity

item.title: The GNU Movement and Linux
item.description: Unix closed; Stallman built free userland; Torvalds filled the kernel gap — GPL kept the combination open

item.title: Virtual Memory and Multitasking
item.description: Time-sharing needs isolation — virtual memory gives every process the illusion of owning the machine

item.title: Containers and Modern OS Isolation
item.description: Full VMs buy strong isolation at heavy cost — namespaces and cgroups share one kernel and isolate almost everything else

item.title: From Machine Code to Assembly
item.description: Raw binary is what the CPU runs — assembly is the first readability layer, still one instruction per mnemonic

item.title: High-Level Languages: FORTRAN, COBOL, Lisp, C
item.description: Four domains forced four abstractions — formula, business prose, symbolic lists, systems close to the metal

item.title: Compilers, JIT, and Modern Language Runtimes
item.description: AOT compiles once without runtime facts; JIT waits for hot paths — and garbage collection shifts cost into the runtime

item.title: Real-Time Systems and Deterministic Scheduling
item.description: Throughput and fairness are not deadlines — hard real-time needs bounded worst-case timing, not average speed

item.title: Real-Time Systems in Practice
item.description: Sense–compute–actuate on a fixed budget — avionics and industrial control where Phase 3’s speed tricks become timing enemies

item.title: Buses 101
item.description: A shared bus can do one transaction at a time — that ceiling forces everything after

item.title: From ISA Bus to PCI to PCIe
item.description: Skew killed the wide parallel bus; point-to-point serial is how we escaped

item.title: PCIe Deep Dive
item.description: Intent rides TLPs; reliability and signaling sit below — the stack that replaced the shared bus

item.title: Memory Buses
item.description: DDR bought bandwidth; latency barely moved — banks and channels hide the wait

item.title: The Memory Wall
item.description: CPU speed and DRAM latency diverged for decades — caches hide the gap; they do not close it

item.title: The Clock Speed Wall
item.description: Frequency hit heat — so the industry went wide (cores, then fabrics) instead of faster clocks

item.title: Interconnects at Scale
item.description: Once compute is many chips, the path between them is the next wall — dedicated links, fewer copies

item.title: Serial Links and the First Machine-to-Machine Connections
item.description: Point-to-point serial links connect exactly two ends — the ceiling that forced packet switching

item.title: ARPANET and Packet Switching
item.description: Bursty computer traffic broke circuit switching — ARPANET proved packets and shared links could work

item.title: Ethernet and the Local Area Network
item.description: Shared cable, no central arbiter — CSMA/CD solved the LAN collision constraint; switches later removed it

item.title: TCP/IP and the Modern Internet Stack
item.description: How internet protocols stacked and why — layers, flag day, apps on an unreliable substrate — not a catalog

item.title: Datacenter Networking and RDMA
item.description: Inside one controlled fabric, kernel copies become the tax — RDMA and topology buy back the wire

item.title: Usenet, Archie, Gopher, and the Pre-Web Internet
item.description: Find, then talk — Usenet, Archie, Gopher, IRC, and the consumer portals that packaged both

item.title: Google's Big Data Infrastructure — Why They Won
item.description: Web-scale data forced failure-as-normal storage, then a programming model that hid the cluster — GFS, MapReduce, Bigtable

item.title: Kubernetes and Container Orchestration at Scale
item.description: Thousands of containers failing routinely force declarative desired state and a continuous reconciliation loop

item.title: The Machine Learning Software Stack
item.description: Between a model and silicon sits a stack that turns tensors into distributed training — and hits the interconnect wall

item.title: What '7nm' Actually Means
item.description: Node names stopped tracking one physical length — density and pitch are the physics; the label is a generation

item.title: Photolithography
item.description: Diffraction forces shorter wavelengths — EUV’s mirrors and tin plasma are what kept feature sizes moving

item.title: FinFET to GAA
item.description: Short-channel leakage killed planar shrink — wrap the gate (FinFET), then wrap it all around (GAA)

item.title: Moore's Law
item.description: Moore’s observation was economic component count — transistor count still climbs; clocks and cost-per-transistor tell different stories

item.title: Chiplets & Advanced Packaging
item.description: Yield falls with die area — split into chiplets and buy back bandwidth with advanced packaging

item.title: Why GPUs Exist
item.description: Graphics gave an embarrassingly parallel workload — SIMT hardware followed, then general compute found the same shape

item.title: CUDA Cores, Warps, and Occupancy
item.description: SIMT maps onto SMs and warps — lockstep wins until divergence, occupancy hides memory stalls

item.title: GPU Memory Hierarchy
item.description: Thousands of threads force bandwidth over DDR — HBM stacks memory beside compute

item.title: Tensor Cores
item.description: Matrix multiply-accumulate became the dominant AI op — so hardware made it a first-class primitive

item.title: Multi-GPU Scaling
item.description: One GPU is finite — interconnect between GPUs becomes the next wall

item.title: Why Matrix Multiply Reshaped Chip Design
item.description: AI compute reduces to matmul at scale — specialize silicon for that shape

item.title: Systolic Arrays
item.description: Data pulses through a MAC grid — specialize the whole chip for matmul (TPUs)

item.title: Quantization & Mixed Precision
item.description: Fewer bits per MAC means more MACs in the same power budget — mix precision where accuracy still needs it

item.title: Sparsity in Hardware
item.description: Skip known-zero MACs — but only structured patterns are cheap for dense MAC hardware to exploit

item.title: Interconnect at Datacenter Scale
item.description: Thousands of GPUs — topology and all-reduce matter as much as any chip’s peak FLOPS

item.title: Where It's Headed
item.description: Same pattern forward — chiplets, optics closer to the package, compute nearer memory

item.title: Attention Is All You Need
item.description: Self-attention closed the spine — parallel sequence modeling that maps onto the matmul hardware the journey built

item.title: Who Decides the Wire
item.description: Who names numbers, names, and encodings so heterogeneous networks can interoperate

item.title: Wartime Crypto
item.description: Enigma, Bletchley, and Colossus — why breaking ciphers forced electronic computing

item.title: Privacy, Consent, Identity, Cyber
item.description: Privacy, consent, identity, and cybersecurity as engineering evolution on an open network — not a policy pamphlet

item.title: Visions That Shipped
item.description: Forward links out of the journey — Cisco, Gates, Jobs, GNU+Linus, Elon, Bezos as seeds of kinds that turned stack into lived platforms

item.title: Platform Synthesis
item.description: One high-level stop — a large platform is distributed systems, networking, AI infra, privacy engineering, and software engineering composed

item.title: Timeline
item.description: A condensed chronology from mechanical calculation to modern attention mechanisms

item.title: Glossary
item.description: Key terms used throughout the series, defined precisely
